chapter: Trent's band: Texas, St. Louis and the road east
title: Lee Hilliard, the Hudson telegram and gossip about him
summary: Repeats the story of Hilliard and the stolen telegram and what St. Louis men thought of Hudson.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: So really, until you got Hayes Pillars, you really didn't have an out-
We had Lee Hilliard.
Where did you get-- when did you get Hilliard?
That's what I--
He's in while you're still in Texas? I thought you didn't get him until you came back down into Texas again? He's only on that one picture--no, I don't think he's in any of the pictures.
I don't think he's on any picture, not even the one with the overcoats. That has Dan Minor.
I have a picture of Hilliard, because I got a picture of Hilliard with Stuff's band up in Buffalo, he was playing in the trumpet section. He played trumpet and alto.
Right.
He's from San Antoino; right?
San Antonio.
You had him in the band--

he had to be replacing somebody in the saxophone section, because weren't you telling me one time that the reason--somebody else was supposed to come in the band but everybody was crazy about Lee because he could play trumpet and sax, and that was the reason. There was somebody else that they were supposed to get in the band.
No. That happened with the George Hudson case.
We were after another trumpet player.

That was Roy, you were trying to Roy Elder and George Hudson stole the telegram. He didn't give it to Roy, he kept the telegram himself and came in Roy's place. That's why you were trying to get Roy Elder and you got Hudson instead.
That's right.
I knew about that. Pillars told me that.
In fact, I think Hudson admitted it himself.
He almost got sent back
and I was so happy to have another young guy close to my age--I think he was even younger than I am-- that I kept him.
He wasn't no great musician though; was he?
He was a pretty good musician.
Some of the guys weren't crazy about him; the guys around St. Louis weren't all that crazy about him. He didn't leave Jeter's band under the most favorable conditions.
He didn't?
You know, like he slipped out. He was an agitating kind of guy, there are stories. That doesn't concern us anyway.
Pillars was telling me one thing or somebody else was saying something.
He was rehearsing with Stuie Jackson's band when he was still supposed to be working with Pillars.
I didn't know that.
